Free beta

Play KickMaths for free during beta.

Families and schools can try the current game for free. A paid version is coming soon, with pricing and launch details to be announced later.

Play the free betaSend beta feedback

What can you try in the beta?

Primary maths for Years 1–6

Practise times tables, written calculations, fractions and other skills organised around England’s primary maths curriculum.

Football matches and earned rewards

Answer maths questions, score goals, earn XP and use game credits to customise a player. Credits are earned through practice.

Reports and reading preferences

Review topic evidence and example questions, try dyslexia-friendly mode and choose reduced motion in the game.

Start without a payment or activation code.

Choose Play the free beta, create a nickname profile and select a suitable practice year. No payment or activation code is needed during beta. Each pupil should use a separate profile so their learning records stay separate.

Help us improve KickMaths.

The game is still being developed. If a question, written method or screen does not work as expected, tell us which activity you were using, your device and what happened. Ideas from pupils, parents and teachers help shape the next version.

Send beta feedback

Our feedback form opens in Google Forms. Please leave out children’s personal details.

Keep a backup of progress.

Progress and reports are saved in the browser used to play. There is no automatic cloud save. Use Backup in the grown-up area before clearing browser data or moving to another device.

Frequently asked questions

Is the beta free for schools as well as families?

Yes. The current beta is free for both families and schools. No payment or activation code is needed.

Will there be a paid version?

Yes. A paid version is coming soon. We will announce its pricing and launch details later.

How can I report a bug or suggest an improvement?

Use the feedback button on this page or inside the game. Include the maths activity, device and what happened, without children’s personal details.
